Use this branch after [installation](installation.qmd) for ordinary HFSS
Eigenmode, Driven Modal/Terminal and Q3D. These families use direct GDS imports
with explicit layer/object bindings. They do not automatically consume the
Xmon GeometryPlan or its EPR catalogue. Q2D has its own explicit
[cross-section lesson](aedt-q2d.qmd).

The public specimen and executable notebook sources belong to
[OrPen's pinned CPW group](../examples.qmd#public-inputs). Its CPW is 500 µm
long, with a 10 µm signal, 6 µm gaps, 80 µm grounds and a 500 µm substrate.
Those are example design inputs, not measured device geometry or universal
solver settings. The GDS contains three metal rectangles and the substrate
area. The PDK supplies the layer pairs and material/library facts.

## Make the shared source and mapping

```python
from pathlib import Path
import gdsfactory as gf
import orpen_sc_pdk
from orpen_sc_pdk.tech import LAYER
from orpen_sc_pdk.materials import get_material_records
from scgsim.aedt import LayerImport, ObjectBinding, PdkMaterial

orpen_sc_pdk.activate()
coupon = gf.Component()
coupon << gf.components.rectangle(size=(500.0, 10.0), centered=True,
                                  layer=LAYER.D0_TOP_M1_DRAW)
upper = coupon << gf.components.rectangle(size=(500.0, 80.0), centered=True,
                                          layer=LAYER.D0_TOP_M1_DRAW)
upper.movey(51.0)
lower = coupon << gf.components.rectangle(size=(500.0, 80.0), centered=True,
                                          layer=LAYER.D0_TOP_M1_DRAW)
lower.movey(-51.0)
coupon << gf.components.rectangle(size=(500.0, 182.0), centered=True,
                                  layer=LAYER.D0_SUBSTRATE_AREA)
source_gds = Path(".artifacts/public-cpw-source/cpw.gds")
source_gds.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
coupon.write_gds(source_gds, with_metadata=False)

records = get_material_records()
materials = {
    name: PdkMaterial(name, records[name]["material_kind"],
                      records[name]["is_superconducting"],
                      records[name]["aedt_library_name"])
    for name in ("vacuum", "Si", "Nb")
}
layer_imports = (
    LayerImport(1, 0, "D0_TOP_M1", 0.0, 0.0),
    LayerImport(201, 0, "D0_SUBSTRATE", -500.0, 0.0),
)
object_bindings = (
    ObjectBinding("D0_TOP_M1_1", 1, "signal", "Nb"),
    ObjectBinding("D0_TOP_M1_2", 1, "ground", "Nb"),
    ObjectBinding("D0_TOP_M1_3", 1, "ground", "Nb"),
    ObjectBinding("D0_SUBSTRATE_4", 201, "substrate", "Si"),
)
ground_objects = ("D0_TOP_M1_2", "D0_TOP_M1_3")
```

The declared imported object names follow this pinned specimen/import order;
SCGSim requires exact native readback later, not a semantic guess from a similar
name. Zero metal Z thickness here means HFSS sheets. Q3D replaces that interval
with finite thickness in its lesson. Material identity remains Nb even though
the superconducting approximation lowers to PEC. Si and vacuum reference the
PDK's exact AEDT library names; SCGSim does not manufacture their properties.

Read `layer_imports` and `object_bindings` together. A binding's role tells the
family which imported conductor is signal or ground, while `material_id` keeps
PDK provenance. Each GDS layer/datatype pair must match the declared imports.
Inspecting the coupon is source observation only; actual native object type,
material and assignments are read back during execution.

The native six-face padding order is `(+X, -X, +Y, -Y, +Z, -Z)`, matching PyAEDT.
It differs from the Q2D four-value order. Use the spec's documented order rather
than copying comments from a different family.

Keep `source_gds`, `materials`, `layer_imports`, `object_bindings` and
`ground_objects` in this preparation session. Continue to
[ordinary Eigenmode](aedt-eigenmode.qmd), [Driven Modal](aedt-driven-modal.qmd),
[Driven Terminal](aedt-driven-terminal.qmd), or [Q3D](aedt-q3d.qmd).
This shared lesson authors no component notebook; the canonical OrPen notebooks
remain the execution source for their complete consumer workflow.
